notes: Measured on main 18862da73a6b87966c52014c9ec82c5389d898cb (grit 0.6.0) with grit-bench daily on a 4-vCPU VM (Intel Xeon, 15.6 GB); grit is compared with git version 2.43.0 only (no baseline release). The report is dated by the run's start day (UTC 2026-11-18). Harness issues, in order: (1) the first full invocation aborted in setup at clone/http@synth-10k because grit-http-server was not built; it was built and the full run restarted with --offline --http-server. (2) The second full invocation aborted at remote/rename@many-refs ('grit produced no timed samples'), and grit-bench writes no report when any scenario errors, so nothing from it was reused. (3) The published numbers therefore come from running each of the 172 scenarios in its own 'grit-bench daily --offline --http-server ... --only <id>' invocation (default warmups and min-runs; fixtures cached and shared), one at a time with nothing else running, then merging the per-scenario results; remote/rename@many-refs succeeded in this form (488 s). All 172 scenarios completed for both tools; no failures, no skipped scenarios. Because scenarios were run in separate invocations rather than one pass, cross-scenario cache state differs slightly from a single run. The repos table is carried over from the previous report (same pinned fixtures, git.git v2.47.0) because grit-bench daily does not emit one. area keeps grit-bench's native area names (as in previous reports). Per-tool runs/samples_ms/min_ms/max_ms/stddev_ms and the whole detail object come straight from grit-bench; max_rss_kb is peak RSS bytes/1024. grit-bench also flags five extra rows as headline (branch/list-json, branch/merged, log/json-100, pull/rebase, push/force-with-lease); this report marks only the 17 scenarios from the headline table. Noise check against the 2026-11-09 report: 35 scenarios whose grit/git time ratio got >20% worse or memory ratio >30% worse were re-run three more times each (separate invocations, 105 extra runs) and all samples were pooled (median/stddev over all samples; max_rss_kb is the median of the per-invocation peaks): add/dry-run@synth-10k add/update-ignorecase@synth-100k branch/create@many-refs branch/merged@many-refs branch/rename@many-refs bundle/verify@synth-10k cat/blob@git-git commit/dry-run@synth-10k config/get@small config/set@small diff/staged@deep-tree diff/staged@synth-100k diff/worktree@big-blobs diff/worktree@deep-tree diff/worktree@synth-100k diff/worktree@synth-10k fsck/full@git-git gc/pack-refs@synth-10k init/empty@small log/json-100@git-git log/oneline-100@synth-100k merge/content-both-sides@wide-20k notes/add@synth-10k notes/list-n100@synth-10k notes/list@synth-10k rebase/onto@git-git remote/list@small resolve/head-n@git-git revs/author-n50@deep-history rm/dry-run@synth-10k show/head@big-blobs show/head@synth-10k stash/list@synth-10k status/dirty@synth-10k tag/create@many-refs .
